body:
## Problem

An unnamed top-level `across(...)` in a Margin summary cannot receive its
columns and function through an enclosing wrapper's populated dots. This is
distinct from #1138's selector inside an inline function: unnamed top-level
`across()` takes dplyr's expansion path, whose evaluation timing is fixed by
ADR 0019.

```r
data <- data.frame(g = c("a", "a", "b"), x = 1:3)
ordinary <- function(...) dplyr::summarise(data, dplyr::across(...), .by = g)
margin <- function(...) summarize_with_margins(data, dplyr::across(...), .by = g)
ordinary(.cols = "x", .fns = sum) # x: 3, 3
margin(.cols = "x", .fns = sum)   # '...' used in an incorrect context
```

Preserve dplyr's function-factory evaluation timing as well as values. With
`.fns = factory()` and a factory that records `dplyr::n()` then adds it to
each `sum(x)`, ordinary dplyr invokes it once with 0 and returns 3, 3. A
runtime wrapper around the helper instead invokes it per group and changes
the result, so merely deferring the whole call is insufficient.

Reproduced on main `a563444f831d793c08c15e94510ff09e3377c300`, R 4.6.1,
dplyr 1.2.1, rlang 1.3.0 and tidyselect 1.2.1 on aarch64 macOS. The independent
main reproduction was run from a source archive; no relevant test was skipped.
All-state issue and PR searches for `"across" "forward"` and
`"dots" "across"` found no matching report. #1138 and PR #1149 address the
inline-function boundary and retain this top-level expansion path.

comments.body: Implemented in #1172. Verification and independent Standards/Spec review records are linked from the PR.

title: [P2] Preserve forwarded selectors in top-level across expansion
